questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How people complain and which businesses handle it badly
The oldest objects and complaint letters in the British Museum
How to get a job in customer service with no experience
Why British people are too polite to complain in restaurants
questions.why: Sam and Rob discuss complaining and customer service with ideas from Giles Hawke.

questions.q: Why does Rob say he never complains?
options: He always gets good service
He finds it too embarrassing
It never works
He doesn't have time
questions.why: He says, 'I'm British! I never complain... It's just too embarrassing.'

questions.q: What does Sam say about British people today?
options: They have stopped complaining completely
They only complain online
They are complaining more than before
They complain less than other countries
questions.why: Sam says it seems the British are complaining more than they used to.

questions.q: According to Giles Hawke, which sectors have more problems than average?
options: Travel, retail, leisure and the hotel industry
Banking, food, fashion and online shopping
Education, health and the charity sector
Public services, telecoms, transport and services
questions.why: He lists public services, telecommunications, transport and service sector.

questions.q: What does Rob mean by 'inherent challenges' in these sectors?
options: Problems that come from the nature of the business
Problems caused by lazy or badly trained staff
Problems that are quick and cheap for companies to fix
Problems that only happen in bad weather or at holidays
questions.why: He explains an inherent problem is part of the nature of the thing itself.

questions.q: Which sectors does Giles Hawke say are performing well?
options: Transport and public services
Travel, retail and leisure
Telecoms and transport
Only the service sector
questions.why: He says travel, retail and leisure appear to be performing well.

questions.q: How are most complaints still made?
options: On social media
By email
In person at a shop
By phone or by letter
questions.why: He says over 58% of complaints are made by phone or letter.

questions.q: When do people tend to use social media to complain?
options: Always as their very first step, before phoning
Only for small problems that aren't worth a letter
When their complaint wasn't dealt with the first time
When they want to praise a company for good service
questions.why: It is used as an escalation point if people aren't getting what they want dealt with first.
